name: read-url
description: Extract clean, complete markdown from any web page — articles, docs, READMEs, blog/social posts, academic papers. Also use as a fallback when curl returns noisy HTML or WebFetch returns truncated, summarized, or refused results.

findings.excerpt: 1. **Raw `.md` / `.txt` / plain-text URL** → `curl -sL <url>` (already clean, no HTML to strip)
3. **Docs page** → try `curl -sL <url>.md`. Mintlify and other docs platforms serve clean markdown on the `.md` route — if the response is `text/markdown`, you'
4. **Blog / newsletter / multi-post index** → try RSS first: `curl -sL <url>/feed` (also `/rss`, `/feed.xml`, `/atom.xml`, `/index.xml`). Most static-site gener
5. **Generic site** (articles, docs, tech blogs, unknown) → `npx defuddle parse <url> --markdown` — see `references/defuddle.md`

Extract clean readable content from generic web pages via `npx defuddle`. Removes navigation, ads, sidebars — returns only the main content as markdown.
npx defuddle parse <url> --markdown
npx defuddle parse <url> --property title
npx defuddle parse <url> --property description
npx defuddle parse 'https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector' --markdown
